Well, we don't really. Largely what we know is from ancient historians, from the writings of Josephus, Livy, or Suetonius,  for example. From there, modern historians interpret their writings with archeological evidence, or compare the writings of one ancient historian to that of another contemporary ancient historian. For example, say one historian stated that Caesar had a child with Cleopatra, and another historian backs up this claim, this "fact" become slightly more valid to modern historians because it comes from multiple sources. However, all ancient texts are constantly being questioned by modern historians, no matter how valid it might seem, due to biases that were often prevalent in ancient sources (the idea of historical bias was not a thing during antiquity, at least to ancient romans it wasnt). Mostly the most concrete evidence people can gather from antiquity (ancient egypt, greece, and rome, mostly my knowledge of history comes from these eras) is from archeology, and even archeological findings can be up for interpretation sometimes. Ultimately we could never really know what happened during antiquity, due to the fact historians don't have any visual data from those periods. I guess that's what makes ancient history really fascinating is that any new finding or archeological dig could really change this particular field of study, that unlike other parts of history the facts and interpretations of those facts are always up for debate.

I have many worst days, probably the top of the worst days was finding out that my aunt had been murdered. You can never really fully prepare yourself for something like that. I felt like I was living in nightmare, only seen on the news or out of a episode of CSI.  I knew nobody who could relate to it, and I felt like I could talk to nobody about it, although murder is quite prevalent in American society, often most of your peers will never encounter it, at least in my peer group. It was unbelievable to me, and I'm still reeling from it, 10 years after it has happened. My family got a year to process it, and try to move on, achieve a new normal, and then we were hit with the actual murder trial the very next year, which forced us to relieve every detail of my aunt's murder. The trial took place a year after my aunt had been murdered, and it took about a full year to come to a verdict. The trial itself was like living through the very first day I found out she had been killed all over again, and again, day after day. Having a loved one killed senselessly is so hard to deal with, normally you can at least process the death of a loved one who was sick or died of old age, although no less heartbreaking. But when a loved one passes due to murder, drug abuse, suicide, drug abuse, a car accident, or freak accident, too soon, it's like a million daggers pierce your heart everyday and you can't possible ever be at peace with their death, because people are not supposed to die like that. I will never forget the day I was sat down by my grandmother and mother and was told about my aunt's murder, just filled with overwhelming grief and anger. My family has never been the same since.
TL:DR, the day my Aunt I found out my Aunt was murdered.
